title: ops-midnight-scrapbook-and-esc-summaries-2027-02-01
content:
Midnight Ops Scrapbook — 2027-02-01 (UTC)

Shift summary (00:00–08:00 UTC):
- Primary focus: investigate increased tail latency and 5xx spike from hosted API cluster in us-west-2 between 00:12–01:03 UTC.
- Total incidents: 1 P1 (elevated error rate for text-gen r/w path), 2 P2 follow-ups (slow cache flushes, alert noise).
- Escalations: Pager escalated to eng-sre on-call at 00:14 UTC, on-call paged infra-owner (Marco) at 00:20 UTC.

Timeline/what we saw:
- 00:11 UTC: Alert triggered — 95th percentile latency > 1200ms and error rate for /v1/generate rose from 0.2% -> 4.8%.
- 00:13 UTC: Correlated with spikes in redis slot eviction metrics on host pool (redis-evict-rate up 4x).
- 00:15 UTC: Canary traffic showed increased token-level retry errors; tail latency concentrated on requests > 1024 tokens.
- 00:22 UTC: Degraded instances replaced by autoscaler but replacement lag ~120s due to node provisioning; temporary throughput drop.
- 00:30 UTC: Applied short-term mitigation: moved small percentage (~10%) of heavy long-seq traffic to lower-memory model variant (rwd-gen-7b-q4f32) via routing override. Latency returned to baseline for routed subset.
- 00:42 UTC: Discovered a recently-merged config change in infra repo that lowered Redis maxmemory-policy from volatile-lru to allkeys-lru (PR #345) — this increased eviction churn for KV cache, causing more cache misses and repo-level regen requests.
- 01:03 UTC: Full rollout pause and partial rollback of that config to previous setting. Error rate back to baseline by 01:10 UTC.

Immediate root-cause hypothesis:
- Change to Redis eviction policy increased churn for caching layer used by KV-prefix cache for long context sessions. Combined with an increase in long-seq requests and delayed node provisioning, this produced a transient cascade of cache misses -> backend load -> higher latency and errors.

Quick wins / actions taken during shift:
- Hotfix: config rollback (rolled-by: Marco Li) at 00:45 UTC, verified via metrics and prometheus query (slo-layer:kv_cache_miss_rate).
- Traffic steering: routing override to rwd-gen-7b-q4f32 for heavy requests (applied 00:30, reverted 01:05 after stability confirmed).
- Autoscaler tweak: temporarily lowered min-unready-threshold to speed provisioning for the cluster (tuned by Sophie Nguyen).
- Incident annotated in incident channel with timeline and initial RCA notes.

Runbook gaps & proposed edits (actionable):
- Runbook: redis-eviction-runbook lacks a section for "eviction-policy rollout checklist". Add steps to validate cache hit-rate under synthetic long-seq load before global rollout. (owner: Sophie, due: 2027-02-04)
- Add a verification query and dashboard tile: kv_cache_hit_rate_by_seq_len to catch long-context regressions early. (owner: Aisha, due: 2027-02-03)
- Autoscaler doc: clarify node provisioning SLOs and how to temporarily adjust unready thresholds during P1s. (owner: Platform Eng doc owners, linked: SRE-4821)

Follow-ups & action items (ordered by priority):
1) Postmortem draft (INC-2027-02-01) — collect logs, timeline, and RCA snippets. Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2027-02-03.
2) Runbook edit: eviction-policy rollout checklist + pre-rollout load test. Owner: Sophie Nguyen. Due: 2027-02-04.
3) Dashboard: kv_cache_hit_rate_by_seq_len. Owner: Aisha. Due: 2027-02-03.
4) Infra PR review: add automated pre-merge check to detect eviction-policy changes for clusters with prefix-caching. Owner: Marco Li. Ref: PR #345. Due: 2027-02-05.
5) Reconcile alerts: tune alert thresholds to focus on combined latency+error signals for >1k token requests to reduce noise. Owner: Eng-SRE. Due: 2027-02-07.

Notes to next shift (handoff bullets):
- Priority 1: Finish postmortem draft and publish stub in /incidents (INC-2027-02-01). Share with SRE lead before 12:00 UTC.
- Priority 2: Keep an eye on cache miss rate for us-west-2 (dashboard link in artifacts). If kv_cache_miss_rate > 2% sustained for 10m, consider re-routing heavy traffic to replica region or model variant.
- Manual checks: confirm autoscaler settings in us-west-2 are back to baseline after morning maintenance window; revert temporary provisioning tweak after stabilization.
- Watch for noise: a low-severity alert (ALERT-redis-eviction-spike) may still fire on noisy metrics — do not escalate unless accompanied by sustained error-rate increase on /v1/generate.

Misc observations & brain-dump:
- We should quantify how many user sessions are long-seq (>=1024 tokens) and whether sticky-session caching is effective for those. Might be a good Optimize feature opportunity.
- Consider adding an automatic canary that simulates 1% long-seq traffic during config rollouts to validate eviction behaviour.

Raw links & refs:
- Incident ticket: INC-2027-02-01
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/345
- Runbook (draft edit target): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/redis-eviction-runbook
- Slack thread: slack://channel?team=T12345&id=C0ABCDEF0/thread_ts/1675238400.000100

Closing notes:
- Shift owner: Aisha Patel (overnight primary).
- Secondary: Marco Li (infra), Sophie Nguyen (autoscaler/telemetry).
- Confidence: medium — rollback fixed the immediate symptom but we still need a short postmortem to confirm no latent degradation and to close follow-ups.

Notes to self (untidy):
- Check if we can add a synthetic long-seq generator to the chaos harness.
- Remind release-engineering to include eviction-policy flag in the change-notes checklist.

End of shift snapshot.
